quest.title: Experiment Phase: Uncontrolled Parameters
quest.description: There seems to be a groaning Sumeru researcher in the suburbs of Liyue. This isn't the first time you've seen a groaning researcher, but you can't help but wonder what he's here for...

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: There's no way I'm gonna finish this... Guess I have no choice but to reduce the scale of my experiment. Let me think... How should I explain this to my mentor?

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: "Ohh, my experiment is way too hard to conduct! It's impossible to find the right materials, and I still failed after trying everything I could to build an ideal experiment environment!"

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Ugh, what a lame excuse... I'm sure my mentor won't have any of that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe you should just tell him up front that you can't complete this project, then come up with a new proposal!

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Wh—Whoa... Don't just join the conversation when someone's talking to themselves!

dialogues.speaker: Jami
dialogues.text: Oh hey, it's you! Do you still remember me? I'm Jami, an Amurta researcher.

choices.text: Oh, you're the one who had a hard time with your thesis proposal...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Yep, that's me. The Amurta researcher who was tormented by his thesis proposal and was this close to seeing the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: *sigh* Anyway, thank you for that suggestion, but as things currently stand, I'm pretty much past the point of no return... If I discontinue this project, my mentor would no doubt skin me alive...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: And that won't be all. He'll leave me to dry and turn me into a specimen, then place me inside the Amurta labs. My label would say "Jami, who failed to live up to his mentor's expectations."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like the start of another urban legend at the Akademiya... Would mentors really do that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's way too exaggerated.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Heh, I guess becoming a specimen wouldn't be too bad... I can at least serve as a warning to my juniors...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, he's become so depressed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why can't you just stop? You shouldn't force yourself to do something you can't do.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: It's complicated... and it's not really impossible to do either. I conducted a similar experiment in the past and even obtained some workable data...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's great! Just continue working on your experiment then!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: *sigh* But everything went downhill from there. My previous experiment was such a huge success that my Darshan began having high hopes for my project. Even my mentor gave me a few compliments.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: "You can do it Jami, I believe in you!" ...Who would've thought that cranky old man would say something like that?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Yeah, I felt truly honored by their kindness and made an impulsive decision to turn my research project into an unprecedented success.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Our Darshan had just received some new funds at that time.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: So I came here and built the best possible experimental site. I used the most advanced building materials and bought top-tier observation equipment at great expense.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: As I worked on constructing the site, I couldn't help but set the highest standards for everything.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon gets it! It's like walking into a restaurant and saying "Just bring up all your best dishes!" when ordering.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Exactly! I was thoroughly won over by that feeling. Before I knew it, the costs began growing exponentially as the scale of my experiment increased.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: The experiment has developed to a point where it's impossible for me to complete, and the sheer cost of maintaining the site makes it difficult to hire additional assistance...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: But if I scale down my experiment, the matra would accuse me of not using the funds completely and pocketing the extra Mora for myself...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Haha, maybe I should just turn myself in before the matra start suspecting... Oh, and before that, I have to enjoy one last meal at Lambad's Tavern.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Just bring up all your best dishes!"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, can you take us with you? No, no, wait, are you sure there's nothing else you can do to save your experiment?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just get to the point and tell us what's troubling you!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: I need more Mora...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, is that a butterfly over there? Let's go check it out!

choices.text: Looks like a flying lizard to me!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Wait, don't go! Hear me out, please! I need the Mora to hire observers who can help with the experiment!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: If you don't mind helping, I wouldn't have to hire extra observers. After the experiment ends, I can simply sell as much equipment as I can and use that Mora as your compensation...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmph. Whatcha think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's help him then.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But what exactly do "observers" of your experiment do?

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: My project is centered on the defense deficiencies of various creatures. Collecting data requires you to engage in strategic combat while taking pictures.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon kinda gets why it's expensive to hire observers now.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Yeah, it is a little dangerous, so you really don't have to help... Just remember to place some flowers before my specimen if you ever pass by the Amurta lab...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, alright, we're pros at fighting monsters! But taking pictures while fighting sounds like a lot of trouble...

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: Don't worry, because this is where my Fayz Potion comes into play!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: This potion only works inside the experimental site. Drinking it will allow you to subjectively feel as if time has slowed down.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: There's no guarantee that you'll be able to dodge every single attack, haha. But at least you'll have enough time to adjust the angle before taking a picture.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks he means: "Injury is unavoidable, but please make sure the photos are good!"

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: With how skilled the both of you look, I'm sure you'll be fine.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: But compared to high-quality pictures, your safety always comes first. I mean it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll be careful!

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: *sob* My entire academic career is in your hands... I'm counting on you!

choices.text: But everyone's so nice to you.

response.speaker: Jami
response.text: I'm that researcher whose proposal got rejected twice and couldn't get started on his experiment... They called me the "groaning Akademiya researcher" Jami.
